record.body: A soundscape is everything audible in a place over a period of time, and soundscape ecology studies it as a whole while keeping its three layers distinct. Biophony is the sounds living organisms make: animal calls, songs, and choruses. Geophony is the sounds of the earth itself: wind, rain, thunder, running water, and waves. Anthrophony is the sounds humans make: traffic, machinery, aircraft, music, and voices. The layers are cross-linked, because animals must communicate through geophony and anthrophony, and because each layer shapes the others, but they are never blurred into one undifferentiated noise: every record in this pair states which layer or layers it covers, so a reader can always tell a bird from the wind behind it and from the road beyond that.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'What a Soundscape Is: Three Layers, Never Blurred'
import math
BIO = 55
GEO = 50
ANTH = 60
tot = 10 * math.log10(10 ** (BIO / 10.0) + 10 ** (GEO / 10.0) + 10 ** (ANTH / 10.0))
dom = 'biophony' if BIO >= GEO and BIO >= ANTH else ('geophony' if GEO >= ANTH else 'anthrophony')
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Biophony: %.1f decibels' % BIO)
print('Geophony: %.1f decibels' % GEO)
print('Anthrophony: %.1f decibels' % ANTH)
print('Combined soundscape level: %.1f decibels' % tot)
print('Dominant layer: ' + dom)
print('Layers are mixed in arithmetic but kept distinct in description.')
demo.expected_output:
Record: What a Soundscape Is: Three Layers, Never Blurred
Biophony: 55.0 decibels
Geophony: 50.0 decibels
Anthrophony: 60.0 decibels
Combined soundscape level: 61.5 decibels
Dominant layer: anthrophony
Layers are mixed in arithmetic but kept distinct in description.
